solutions.check: grid and clues read from the FT's printable PDF, its numbering matching the clue list; every fifteensquared answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Neat deposit?

parts.note: neat is an old word for cattle, so a neat deposit is what a cow leaves in a field, not something tidy

explanation.walkthrough: 'Neat' looks like tidy, but it is the old word for cattle, as in neatsfoot oil.
explanation.definitionFit: A dropping left by a cow is a deposit made by neat, that is, by cattle.

clue.text: Firm beginning to venture into a lot of quaint cooking producing foreign dish

parts.note: Co. is the abbreviation for company, a firm

indicators.note: into means the first letter goes inside the shortened word
cooking means the letters are worked up together into something new
a lot of means most of the word, so it loses its last letter
the beginning of a word is its first letter, here of venture

explanation.surface: A company venturing into quaint cuisine, turning out a foreign dish.
explanation.walkthrough: V goes into QUAIN (quaint minus T) and 'cooking' rearranges QUAINV into QAUVIN, after CO.
explanation.definitionFit: This French chicken stew braised in red wine is a foreign dish.

clue.text: A town yet to be disturbed about dead bird

indicators.note: about means the mixed letters go round the dead letter
to be disturbed means the letters of those three words are thrown into disorder

explanation.surface: A town still to be shaken by a dead bird.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to be disturbed' rearranges ATOWNYET, which wraps round D.
explanation.definitionFit: An American breed of domestic chicken is a kind of bird.

clue.text: Help needed around river that's dry

indicators.note: around means the help word encloses the letter

parts.note: aid means help

explanation.surface: Aid sent to a river region that has gone dry.
explanation.definitionFit: Parched land with almost no rain is dry.

clue.text: Short look before chap stirred top of onion soup

indicators.note: short means the word for look is cut off before its final letter

parts.note: to gaze is to look steadily

indicators.note: stirred means the letters of chap are mixed up, like ingredients in a pot
the top of a word is its first letter, here of onion

explanation.surface: A recipe step: glance briefly, then stir before adding the onion to the soup.
explanation.walkthrough: GAZE loses its end to give GAZ; 'stirred' turns CHAP into PACH; 'top of' gives O from onion.
explanation.definitionFit: This cold Spanish tomato dish is a type of soup.

clue.text: A bachelor entertained by European performer of risky feats?

indicators.note: entertained by means held as a guest inside the European's word

parts.note: a Croat is a native of Croatia, a European

explanation.surface: A single man is hosted by a European stunt artist.
explanation.definitionFit: A gymnast who does daring tumbling and balancing performs risky feats.

clue.text: Go to get drink containing European spirit lacking refined flavour

parts.note: go means energy or vigour, like pep

indicators.note: containing means the drink word holds the other letters

parts.note: a pint is a drink of beer

indicators.note: lacking means the refined letter is taken out of the spirit

parts.note: rum is a spirit
U means upper-class, hence refined

explanation.surface: Advice to get a drink containing some European spirit, short on sophisticated taste.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Go' is a noun here (energy), not a verb; 'refined' is the crossword U for upper-class. 'to get' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: A mint oil used to flavour sweets and toothpaste.

clue.text: Feature associated with a set of porcelain

parts.note: the chin is a facial feature

explanation.surface: A distinctive feature of a porcelain service.
explanation.walkthrough: 'associated with' is a link joining the two pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: Fine ceramic tableware is often called by the country it first came from.

clue.text: Batsman maybe getting exercise in single runs

indicators.note: in means the exercise letters go inside the other pieces

parts.note: single means one
PE is physical education, exercise
R is the cricket abbreviation for runs

explanation.surface: A cricketer getting a workout by scoring singles.
explanation.walkthrough: In cricket the first two batsmen in an innings are the openers.
explanation.definitionFit: A cricketer who starts the innings is an example of a batsman, hence 'maybe'.

clue.text: Very small road followed by enthusiast with energy

parts.note: MI (M1) is Britain's first motorway, a road
a nut is a fan or enthusiast
E is the symbol for energy

explanation.surface: A minor road followed by an energetic fan.
explanation.walkthrough: 'followed by' and 'with' are links.
explanation.definitionFit: Tiny, as in minute detail, means very small.

clue.text: Queen facing one performing in ring playing with fire and heat

parts.note: Muhammad Ali was a boxer, who performed in the boxing ring

indicators.note: playing with the word fire means toying with its letters into a new order

explanation.surface: A queen beside a circus performer who plays with fire and heat.
explanation.walkthrough: 'one performing in ring' suggests a circus act, but it is the boxer ALI; 'playing with' rearranges FIRE as FIER. 'and' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: In sport a preliminary round, or heat, decides who goes through to the next stage.

clue.text: Self-confidence is detected in US writer

indicators.note: detected in means the word is found sitting inside the writer's name

parts.note: Edgar Allan Poe was an American writer

explanation.surface: A remark that self-assurance can be spotted in an American author.
explanation.definitionFit: Composure and assurance in bearing are the same as self-confidence.

clue.text: Language employed in tour dubiously

indicators.note: employed in means the letters are used within the run of words that follows

explanation.surface: A language used doubtfully while on a tour.
explanation.definitionFit: The official language of Pakistan, also widely spoken in India.

clue.text: Money-raising event producing ales?

parts.note: jumbling the letters of the word sale produces ales, so the answer read as an instruction makes the clue's last word

explanation.surface: A fundraiser that turns out beer.
explanation.walkthrough: Read as wordplay, the two words are an anagram instruction: muddle S-A-L-E and you get ALES.
explanation.definitionFit: A charity sale of donated secondhand goods is a classic British fundraising event.

clue.text: Dark period, we hear, associated with violent criminal getting honour

indicators.note: we hear means the sound of the dark period word gives a word spelt differently

parts.note: night is the dark period of the day
hood is short for hoodlum, a violent criminal

explanation.surface: A dark era for a violent thug who still receives a title.
explanation.walkthrough: 'associated with' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: The rank of Sir conferred by the sovereign is an honour.

clue.text: Highly emotional feature of church service given time for Catholic

indicators.note: given one letter for another means a swap: the time letter replaces the Catholic letter
given one letter for another means a swap: the time letter replaces the Catholic letter

parts.note: incense is burned during many church services

explanation.surface: Something emotive in a church service, adjusted for a Catholic congregation.
explanation.walkthrough: INCENSE has its C (Catholic) replaced by T (time).
explanation.definitionFit: Strongly felt and passionate describes someone highly emotional.

clue.text: Disturbance of part of body in the last month

parts.note: tum is a colloquial word for the stomach
ult. (ultimo) means of last month in old business letters

explanation.surface: Some bodily upset suffered during the previous month.
explanation.walkthrough: ULT, short for Latin ultimo, is old commercial shorthand for last month. 'in' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: An uproar or commotion is a disturbance.

clue.text: Award received by a hostel requiring renovation? That's abhorrent

indicators.note: received by means the award letters are taken in by the other letters
requiring renovation means those letters need rebuilding into a new order

parts.note: OM is the Order of Merit, a British award

explanation.surface: A rundown hostel given an award: that is disgusting.
explanation.walkthrough: 'requiring renovation' rearranges AHOSTEL into LOATHSE, which takes in OM.
explanation.definitionFit: Detestable or repulsive things are abhorrent.

clue.text: Posh car provided by university lecturer showing forbearance

parts.note: Merc is short for Mercedes, a luxury car
if means provided that

explanation.surface: A university lecturer supplied with a luxury car, being patient.
explanation.definitionFit: Lenient and compassionate people show forbearance.

clue.text: Retired priest accompanied by German church official

indicators.note: retired means withdrawn, going back, so the priest's word is read backwards

parts.note: Rev. is short for Reverend, a priest's title

explanation.surface: A retired cleric and a German companion, both working for a church.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Retired' looks like a description of the priest, but it reverses REV.
explanation.definitionFit: A church caretaker who also attends on clergy in services is a church official.

clue.text: Game in river mostly is destructive

parts.note: RU is rugby union, a game
taken as written

indicators.note: mostly means most of the river's name, missing its last letter

parts.note: the Ouse is a river in England

explanation.surface: A game played in a river, mostly harmful.
explanation.walkthrough: The Ouse is a river in Yorkshire (and another in Sussex). 'is' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Causing ruin or great loss is being destructive.

clue.text: Strongly criticise set dish

parts.note: to pan a play or film is to criticise it harshly
to cake is to set hard, as mud does

explanation.surface: A harsh review of the set menu dish.
explanation.walkthrough: 'set dish' looks like a set menu, but 'set' gives CAKE (harden) and 'dish' is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A flat fried batter dish, served sweet or savoury.

clue.text: Important person with old volunteers raised staple food

parts.note: a pot, or big pot, is an important person

indicators.note: raised in a down clue means the pieces are read upwards, that is backwards

parts.note: TA is the Territorial Army, Britain's volunteer reserve

explanation.surface: A dignitary with old volunteers growing a basic food.
explanation.walkthrough: 'raised' turns O plus TA into ATO.
explanation.definitionFit: A starchy tuber eaten daily in many countries is a staple food.

clue.text: Trust shown by priest in old military unit

indicators.note: in means the priest's name sits inside the unit's letters

parts.note: the BEF, British Expeditionary Force, was sent to France in both world wars
Eli is the priest in the Bible who raised Samuel

explanation.surface: Faith displayed by a chaplain in a historic army unit.
explanation.definitionFit: Faith or confidence in something is trust.

clue.text: Talk at length about origin of rebellion, one based abroad?

indicators.note: about means the long-talk word goes round the letter

parts.note: to expatiate is to speak or write at length

indicators.note: the origin of a word is its first letter, here of rebellion

explanation.surface: Someone abroad holding forth on how a rebellion started.
explanation.walkthrough: R (origin of rebellion) goes inside EXPATIATE.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone living outside their native country is based abroad.

clue.text: Step around back of theatre for quiet

indicators.note: around means the step word encloses the letter

parts.note: a pace is a step

indicators.note: the back of a word is its last letter, here of theatre

explanation.surface: Pacing around the rear of a theatre for some silence.
explanation.definitionFit: Peace and quiet go together: calm stillness.

clue.text: Young woman with no end of swank and style

indicators.note: with no means a letter is taken away from the young woman's word

parts.note: chick is slang for a young woman

indicators.note: the end of a word is its final letter, here of swank

explanation.surface: A young woman with no showing off at all, just class.
explanation.walkthrough: CHICK loses K, the last letter of swank.
explanation.definitionFit: Elegantly fashionable, so it can stand for style or stylishness.

clue.text: By the sound of it, trim fruit

indicators.note: by the sound of it means the trim word said aloud gives a differently spelt word

parts.note: to pare is to trim

explanation.surface: Seemingly a trim, but actually a fruit.
explanation.definitionFit: A sweet juicy tree fruit, narrower at the stalk.

clue.text: Mountain house in state

parts.note: Mount Ida is a mountain in Crete, and another in Turkey

explanation.surface: A mountain home in an American state.
explanation.definitionFit: A northwestern state of the USA.

clue.text: Moving characteristic of farrier's work?

definitions.meaning: done while on the move, without stopping
a farrier shoes horses, so the work is done literally on a hoof

explanation.walkthrough: A farrier is someone who fits horseshoes.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means done in passing while moving, and literally where a farrier works.

clue.text: Very difficult fellow hides in ground

indicators.note: ground means crushed or milled, so these letters are broken up and re-formed

explanation.surface: A fellow concealing himself in a field.
explanation.walkthrough: 'ground' looks like a noun (land) but is the past tense of grind, shuffling F plus HIDESIN.
explanation.definitionFit: A puzzle described as devilish is extremely hard.

clue.text: Soldiers by wood in distressing experience

parts.note: OR stands for other ranks, soldiers who are not officers
deal is fir or pine timber

explanation.surface: Troops in a forest having a terrible time.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: A severe trial or painful test is a distressing experience.
